in_arabic.name: عجم
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عجم مشتق من الجم الذي يعني غير العرب أو الأعاجم، و هو اسم يستخدم للدلالة على الشخص الذي لا يتحدث العربية أو من أصول غير عربية، و في القرآن الكريم، العجم تشير إلى الأمم غير العربية التي تعبد الله تعالى.

in_urdu.name: عجم
in_urdu.meaning: غیر عرب یا غیر مسلم لوگ
in_urdu.long_meaning: عجم نام کا مطلب ہے غیر عرب یا غیر مسلم لوگ، یہ نام ان لوگوں کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو عرب نہیں ہیں یا ان کی زبان عرب نہیں ہے، اور اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا استعمال خاص معنوں میں ہوتا ہے جیسے کہ غیر مسلم یا غیر عرب شخص کے لئے.

in_hindi.name: अजम
in_hindi.meaning: ग़ैर अरबी या ग़ैर मुस्लिम लोग
in_hindi.long_meaning: अजम नाम का अर्थ है ग़ैर अरबी या ग़ैर मुस्लिम लोग, यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो अरब नहीं हैं या जिनकी भाषा अरबी नहीं है, और भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इसका उपयोग विशेष अर्थों में किया जाता है जैसे कि ग़ैर मुस्लिम या ग़ैर अरबी व्यक्ति के लिए.

in_pashto.name: عجم
in_pashto.meaning: غیر عرب یا غیر مسلمان خلک
in_pashto.long_meaning: عجم نوم معنی دا دی چې غیر عرب یا غیر مسلمان خلک، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره استعمالیږي چې عرب نه دي یا د هغوی ژبه عربي نه ده، او په افغان او پښتون دود کې دا د غیر مسلمان یا غیر عرب سړي لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Ajam
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ajam is derived from the Arabic root 'ajm', which means 'to be unclear' or 'to stammer', and refers to non-Arab or non-Muslim people. In Islamic tradition, Ajam is used to describe those who do not speak Arabic or are of non-Arabic origin. The term is mentioned in the Quranic context to refer to non-Arab nations worshiping Allah.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Ajam" has historical and cultural significance in the Islamic tradition, primarily in the context of the Arab conquest of the Persian Empire (633-651 CE). During this period, the term was used to distinguish the indigenous Persian population from the Arab ruling elites. This cultural division persisted for centuries and carries connotations of distinct linguistic, ethnic, and religious identities.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the term "Ajam" can symbolize unity and diversity within the Islamic community. While the label was once used to distinguish and separate the Persian and Arab peoples, it also reminds us that all Muslims, regardless of their origins, share a common faith and spiritual bond. The concept of "Ummah," or the global Islamic community, underscores the idea that we are all interconnected and should strive to transcend ethnic and cultural divides to build a more inclusive and compassionate religious landscape. Thus, the term "Ajam" can inspire us to look beyond our own differences and focus on our shared values and beliefs as Muslims.

historical_references.reference: The term 'Ajam' originated from the Arabic word 'Ajam' meaning 'non-Arabs'. It was used to distinguish Arabs from other peoples in the Middle East, particularly the Persians. The term became widely used during the early Islamic period, as the Arab Muslim conquerors expanded their territory beyond the Arabian Peninsula.
historical_references.context: The term 'Ajam' was used to denote non-Arab Muslims in the Middle East, particularly the Persians, during the early Islamic period.

historical_references.reference: The term 'Ajam' was also used to refer to the inhabitants of the Iranian plateau during the medieval period. It was a general term used to distinguish the Persian-speaking population from the Arab rulers and conquerors.
